clue.text: End of college scarf stuck in elevator — I may come to the rescue

definitions.text: I may come to the rescue

indicators.note: the pieces are said to be stuck inside the elevator, so they go within its letters

parts.note: lift is the British word for an elevator

indicators.note: only the final letter of the word college is wanted

parts.note: a boa is a long fluffy scarf of feathers or fur

explanation.surface: Someone's college scarf has got jammed in a lift, and a voice offers rescue.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is written in the first person: the answer is speaking about itself.
explanation.definitionFit: A boat launched to save people at sea is the thing that comes to a rescue.

indicators.note: the letters sit inside the run of words trouble, thallium

explanation.surface: Thallium is a poisonous metal, so being in trouble with it sounds like a toxic predicament.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something toxic is deadly, able to kill.

parts.note: funny can mean odd or strange
a girl is a young woman

explanation.surface: Describes an odd young woman who nevertheless has a musical talent.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the Broadway show about Fanny Brice, filmed with Barbra Streisand, is a musical.

clue.text: Reason given for climbing Everest, as written on gaudy tee shirt

indicators.note: the first piece is written on top of the second, so it comes before it

parts.note: as can mean since or for the reason that

indicators.note: gaudy suggests something showy and garish, so the letters are jumbled loudly

explanation.surface: A tourist's loud T-shirt quotes a famous mountaineering line.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests the slogan printed on a shirt, but 'gaudy' scrambles TEE SHIRT into ITS THERE. George Mallory, the British climber lost on Everest in 1924, is said to have given this reason.
explanation.definitionFit: The quotation is literally the justification Mallory gave for attempting the mountain.

clue.text: Complaint got from working in metal

indicators.note: letters that are working are moved about and rearranged

explanation.surface: A worker in a metal shop picks up an illness on the job.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a complaint in the medical sense is an illness or disorder.

indicators.note: to comprehend is to include, so the class word holds the chapter letter

parts.note: a sort is a kind or class

explanation.surface: A guide to an English class's syllabus covering one chapter.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym as a verb: to guide someone is to accompany them on the way.

parts.note: Scarborough is a seaside town on the Yorkshire coast of England
fair can mean clean, as in a fair copy

explanation.surface: Promoting a Yorkshire seaside town for its fresh air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'air' looks like part of the resort's selling point but is the definition: a tune.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the traditional English ballad, made famous by Simon and Garfunkel, is a song or tune.

definitions.meaning: the sense of control or obedience kept in a group
the biological sense, a rank in classification, or a group of people such as a religious society

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: keeping things orderly is discipline, and a taxonomic rank is a class.

clue.text: Ravel describing right current for a musical instrument

indicators.note: to describe a shape is to draw round it, so the ravel word goes around the other pieces

parts.note: to ravel is to tangle
I is the symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: Suggests the composer Ravel writing about the current state of musical rights.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ravel' looks like the French composer, which suits the musical surface, but it is the verb meaning to entangle.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the three-sided steel percussion piece struck with a beater is an orchestral instrument.

indicators.note: involved means intricate or tangled, so these letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A setter boasts that one of their clues refers to a college.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a lyceum is a school or college, after Aristotle's school in Athens.

indicators.note: said briefly, the word for take loses its final letter

parts.note: to nick is slang for to steal or take

explanation.surface: An instruction to swallow one's medicine soon.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a tonic is a restorative medicine.

clue.text: Fast-growing conifers ideally spread round end of garden facing one

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go round the garden's final letter
the letters of ideally are spread out into a new order
only the last letter of the word garden is used

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Advice that fast-growing conifers would ideally be planted around the edge of a garden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spread' makes LEYLADI from IDEALLY; 'round' puts it round N, giving LEYLANDI, and 'facing' sets the I for one after it.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: Leyland cypresses are notoriously quick-growing hedge conifers, the cause of many suburban disputes.

clue.text: Military command generating woe, year US got involved

indicators.note: the letters got tangled together and come out in a new order

explanation.surface: A year of American involvement in a war brought misery.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: this parade-ground order tells soldiers to return to their previous position.

clue.text: Romantic poet in past, one thrown out of club

parts.note: by means past, as in walking by

indicators.note: the numeral is ejected from the club word

parts.note: an iron is a golf club
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A Romantic poet of old was once expelled from his club.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: Lord Byron was one of the leading English poets of the Romantic movement.

definitions.meaning: a verb meaning guide or point in a direction
an adjective meaning without deviation, as in a route

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: to steer is to guide, and a straight route is one with no detours.

indicators.note: nervous suggests jittery and agitated, so the letters are shaken up

explanation.surface: A jittery bride or groom at the altar admits pre-wedding nerves.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: marital is the adjective meaning relating to marriage or wedlock.

clue.text: On the other hand, the angina developed

indicators.note: the letters develop into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A doctor's note that a patient's chest pain nevertheless set in.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: this phrase introduces a contrasting thought, just as on the other hand does.

indicators.note: the reversed word is placed inside the power word

parts.note: sway means power or influence

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset means turned upside down, so the word is read bottom to top

parts.note: deep can mean serious or profound

explanation.surface: A grave power cut disrupts a sporting event.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: motorcycle racing on an oval dirt track is a spectator sport.

clue.text: System of exercises I found in full-page book illustrations

indicators.note: the letter is located within the illustrations word

parts.note: plates are full-page illustrations printed separately in a book

explanation.surface: Someone finds an exercise manual illustrated with full-page pictures.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the body-conditioning method devised by Joseph Pilates is a programme of exercises.

indicators.note: the executive word takes on the numerals within it, as a firm takes on staff

parts.note: a suit is slang for a business executive
MM is 2,000 in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A senior executive with a workforce of two thousand.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a summit is the highest point, the peak.

clue.text: Very poor person for all to see in tabloid?

indicators.note: the film-rating letter goes inside the newspaper word

parts.note: a tabloid is a popular newspaper, a paper
U is the British film certificate meaning suitable for everyone

explanation.surface: A destitute person is exposed publicly in the tabloid press.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a pauper is someone extremely poor, living in poverty.

parts.note: P stands for piano, the musical direction for quiet
Aragon is an autonomous region of north-east Spain

explanation.surface: A fashion model lying low somewhere in Spain.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a paragon is a model of excellence, a perfect example.

indicators.note: the word changes its letter order

explanation.surface: Recent alterations reached a central part of something.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: the core of something is its middle or heart.

indicators.note: the card-suit letter is placed inside the correcting word

parts.note: to edit is to correct text
C is the abbreviation for clubs in card games

explanation.surface: Golf clubs or card suits put in the proper sequence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in correct order' reads as one phrase, but 'order' is the definition, as a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: an edict is an official order or decree.

clue.text: Start of abbreviated number trio made a mess of outside

indicators.note: the scrambled letters sit outside the number's letter
messing up the word means rearranging its letters

parts.note: N is a short form of number

explanation.surface: A musical trio bungles the opening of a shortened piece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'made a mess of' turns TRIO into ITRO, and 'outside' puts that round N.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: an informal short word for an introduction or opening section.

clue.text: I attended the Hatter's tea party to protest before race

definitions.text: I attended the Hatter's tea party

indicators.note: the protest word comes ahead of the race word

parts.note: to march is to demonstrate in protest
to hare is to run very fast

explanation.surface: A guest at the Mad Hatter's party, then off to a demonstration and a race.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: in Lewis Carroll's Alice, this character hosts the mad tea party alongside the Hatter.

clue.text: Scornful humour by male fronting band

indicators.note: the male word stands in front of the band word

parts.note: wit is clever humour
he is the male pronoun
a ring is a circular band

explanation.surface: A frontman with a dry, scornful humour leading a music band.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a withering look or remark is one full of contempt.

parts.note: a part is a component

explanation.surface: A component lies broken in bits.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something taken to pieces lies separated, broken up.

indicators.note: the zero letter is placed inside the country

parts.note: Yemen is a country in the Arabian peninsula
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Border guards letting nothing into a country.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the Yeomen of the Guard are the ceremonial bodyguards of the British monarch.

clue.text: Cast a spell on the way in

definitions.meaning: a verb meaning to bewitch or enchant, stressed on the second syllable
a noun meaning a door or gate into a place

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: to enchant someone is to bewitch them, and a doorway is an access point.
